messages:
anita: Kicking off this month's recurring-incident roundup. Goal: identify highest-impact recurring patterns, agree owners and timelines for remediation, and capture any quick wins. Drop short notes or links to postmortems + a proposed owner.

mike-sre: +1. I ran the recurrence scoring across Q4->Q1. Top signals: db-conn-saturation (3.2x baseline), cache-thundering (2.1x), canary/rollout flaps (1.6x), region-link-instability (1.4x). I can dump the CSV if folks want numbers.

maria-eng: please paste the CSV snippet here, mike. we need to decide triage order.

mike-sre: ```
service,recurrence_ratio,incidents
user-api-db,3.2,14
realtime-cache,2.1,9
deploy-canary,1.6,7
region-network,1.4,5
``` 

leo-ops: thanks. suggestion: prioritize by (recurrence_ratio * avg_customer_impact). db wins on both; realtime-cache has fewer incidents but high latency impact.

jordan-platform: agree. proposal: split into 3 tracks
- Track A (P0): db-conn-saturation fixes (short-term mitigation + long-term pool/driver changes)
- Track B (P1): cache-thundering mitigations (TTL smoothing + hot-key protections)
- Track C (P2): deployment/region flakiness cleanup + improved canary gating

maria-eng: I'll take Track A. Immediate steps: 1) add connection pooling jitter/backoff in the client lib, 2) alert threshold tuning, 3) vertical pool sizing for heavy tenants. Target: RFC + PR by 2026-04-15.

anita: ACTION: maria-eng - DB mitigation RFC + plan - due 2026-04-15. Add to the incident follow-up board and tag with #recurring-db.

mike-sre: ACTION: mike-sre - provide prod load histogram and per-tenant top-talkers by 2026-03-31 to inform pool sizing.

leo-ops: I'll own Track B (cache). Quick wins: 1) TTL smoothing via randomized jitter, 2) implement token bucket circuit in front of hot keys. Target: small rollout by 2026-04-08.

jordan-platform: I'll coordinate Track C and push improved rollout gating into the platform. Will sketch canary health score thresholds + automated rollback in the next sprint. ETA: 2026-04-22.

maria-eng: @jordan-platform can you add a checklist to the rollout runbook so oncall can flip the manual rollback quickly if the automation fails?

jordan-platform: yes, will do. adding runbook item and a one-click rollback snippet.

incident-bot: Consolidated postmortems for these incidents are here: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/recurring-q1-2026 (contains links to each PM + TL;DR table)

anita: We should also track ownership in the remediation tracker and mark any action items that are blocked by infra changes.

mike-sre: FYI some DB fixes require driver upgrade that might affect dedicated customers. I'll open a compatibility note and flag in the commit.

leo-ops: Quick low-effort mitigation that helped last time: limit request concurrency per-tenant at the edge. We should consider enabling that as a default for a month as an experiment.

maria-eng: noted. I'll evaluate risk with the client library changes and whether concurrency limits conflict.

anita: OK. summary of agreed items (copied into thread for trackers):
- ACTION: maria-eng - DB mitigation RFC + PR (due 2026-04-15)
- ACTION: mike-sre - prod load histograms & top-ten tenants (due 2026-03-31)
- ACTION: leo-ops - cache jitter + hot-key protection rollout (due 2026-04-08)
- ACTION: jordan-platform - rollout gating + runbook checklist (due 2026-04-22)
- ACTION: mike-sre - compatibility note for driver upgrade (due 2026-04-05)

anita: please add any blockers here. We'll reconvene in two weeks for a quick sync and update the recurring-incident dashboard.

mike-sre: +1. will post a small table with progress next sync. :thumbsup:

leo-ops: ping me if you want me to prototype the token-bucket logic today.

maria-eng: I'll start the RFC tonight and link it here when ready.

jordan-platform: copying these action items into the sprint board now.

anita: thanks everyone. :eyes: If anyone spots a new pattern between now and the next sync, drop it here rather than creating a new thread so we keep continuity.
